concepts.title: Upper respiratory tract anatomy (nose, pharynx, larynx)
concepts.description: Identify and describe the structures of the nose, nasal conchae, pharynx (naso-, oro-, laryngopharynx), and larynx including epiglottis and vocal folds.

concepts.title: Lower respiratory tract anatomy (trachea to alveoli)
concepts.description: Trace the tracheobronchial tree from trachea to terminal bronchioles and alveoli; characterize the respiratory membrane formed by alveolar and capillary walls.

concepts.title: Pleura and intrapleural pressure dynamics
concepts.description: Distinguish visceral and parietal pleura; explain how pleural fluid and negative intrapleural pressure couple lung to chest wall and prevent collapse.

concepts.title: Respiratory muscles and chest wall mechanics
concepts.description: Identify diaphragm, external/internal intercostals, scalenes, and abdominal muscles; describe their roles in inspiration and forced expiration.

concepts.title: Static lung volumes and capacities
concepts.description: Define TV, IRV, ERV, RV, VC, TLC, FRC; know normal values and how they are measured or calculated.

concepts.title: Spirometry and flow-volume loop interpretation
concepts.description: Interpret FVC, FEV1, FEV1/FVC ratio; differentiate obstructive (low ratio) and restrictive (normal/high ratio) patterns using flow-volume loops.

concepts.title: Minute and alveolar ventilation calculations
concepts.description: Calculate minute ventilation (VE = VT × f) and alveolar ventilation (VA = (VT – VD) × f); explain the impact of dead space on gas turnover.

concepts.title: Dead space and Bohr equation
concepts.description: Distinguish anatomical and physiological dead space; apply the Bohr equation (VD/VT = (PaCO2 – PECO2)/PaCO2) to quantify physiological dead space.

concepts.title: Pulmonary compliance and hysteresis
concepts.description: Define compliance (ΔV/ΔP); interpret pressure-volume curves showing hysteresis and the effects of emphysema (increased) vs fibrosis (decreased).

concepts.title: Surfactant and Laplace's law in alveolar stability
concepts.description: State Laplace's law (P = 2T/r) and explain how surfactant reduces surface tension, prevents alveolar collapse and decreases work of breathing.

concepts.title: Airway resistance and Poiseuille's law
concepts.description: Apply Poiseuille's law (R ∝ 1/r⁴) to explain factors affecting resistance; link to bronchial smooth muscle tone, asthma, and bronchodilators.

concepts.title: Work of breathing components
concepts.description: Identify elastic work (lung/chest wall recoil) and resistive work (airway/tissue resistance); recognize conditions that increase each component.

concepts.title: Medullary and pontine respiratory centers
concepts.description: Describe the dorsal respiratory group (DRG) for inspiration, ventral respiratory group (VRG) for forced expiration, and pontine centers (apneustic, pneumotaxic) for pattern modulation.

concepts.title: Peripheral and central chemoreceptors in ventilatory control
concepts.description: Explain how peripheral chemoreceptors (carotid and aortic bodies) sense PO2, PCO2, pH, and central medullary chemoreceptors respond to CSF [H+]; predict ventilatory responses.

concepts.title: Pressure changes during inspiration and expiration
concepts.description: Track alveolar, intrapleural, and transpulmonary pressures during quiet breathing and forced maneuvers; explain pneumothorax consequences.

topics.title: Gas exchange, transport, and blood pH

concepts.title: Respiratory membrane and Fick's law of diffusion
concepts.description: Apply Fick's law (V gas ∝ A × ΔP × D / T) to explain gas exchange; relate changes in surface area, thickness, or pressure gradient to disease (e.g., emphysema, fibrosis).

concepts.title: Oxygen cascade and partial pressure gradients
concepts.description: Trace PO2 from inspired air (≈160 mmHg) to mitochondrial PO2 (<5 mmHg); identify key drop points (alveolar, arterial, capillary).

concepts.title: Alveolar gas equation and ideal PAO2
concepts.description: Calculate ideal alveolar PO2 using PAO2 = (PB – PH2O) × FiO2 – (PaCO2 / R); interpret in hypoventilation and altered FiO2.

concepts.title: Oxygen content and transport in blood
concepts.description: Compute arterial O2 content: CaO2 = (Hb × 1.34 × SaO2) + (0.003 × PaO2); compare dissolved vs. hemoglobin-bound O2 contributions.

concepts.title: Hemoglobin structure and cooperative binding
concepts.description: Describe Hb quaternary structure (α2β2), heme group Fe2+, and T→R conformational change during O2 binding; relate to sigmoidal dissociation curve.

concepts.title: Oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve characteristics
concepts.description: Interpret the sigmoidal curve: plateau at high PO2 (loading), steep at tissue PO2 (unloading); define P50 and its clinical significance.

concepts.title: Bohr effect and modulators of Hb-O2 affinity
concepts.description: Explain how increased PCO2, [H+], temperature, and 2,3-BPG shift the curve right (decreased affinity) and enhance O2 unloading; opposite for left shift.

concepts.title: CO2 transport forms and carbonic anhydrase
concepts.description: List three CO2 transport forms: dissolved (5-10%), carbamino-Hb (20-30%), bicarbonate HCO3- (60-70%); describe role of carbonic anhydrase in RBC.

concepts.title: Cloride shift (Hamburger phenomenon)
concepts.description: Explain the Cl-/HCO3- antiport across RBC membrane to maintain electroneutrality during CO2 loading/unloading; link to plasma chloride changes.

concepts.title: Haldane effect and CO2 dissociation curve
concepts.description: State that deoxygenated hemoglobin has greater affinity for CO2 and H+, facilitating CO2 loading at tissues; interpret the Haldane effect on CO2 transport.

concepts.title: Ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) matching and regional differences
concepts.description: Define V/Q ratio (ideally ~0.8); describe lung zones (West zones) and how gravity affects ventilation/perfusion distribution; calculate alveolar-arterial O2 difference.

concepts.title: Shunt vs. dead space as V/Q abnormalities
concepts.description: Distinguish shunt (perfused but not ventilated, V/Q <1, responds poorly to O2) from dead space (ventilated but not perfused, V/Q >1); give examples.

concepts.title: Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for bicarbonate buffer
concepts.description: Apply pH = pKa + log([HCO3-]/(0.03 × PCO2)) to assess acid-base status; identify normal values (pH 7.4, HCO3- 24 mM, PCO2 40 mmHg).

concepts.title: Respiratory compensation in acid-base disturbances
concepts.description: Predict ventilator response to metabolic acidosis/alkalosis (Kussmaul breathing, hypoventilation) and interpret compensatory changes in PCO2.

concepts.title: Carbon monoxide poisoning and Hb affinity
concepts.description: Explain CO’s high affinity for Hb (~200x O2), left shift of O2 dissociation curve, decreased O2 unloading, and functional anemia; identify cherry-red skin and treatment with 100% O2.

concepts.title: Oral cavity and salivary glands
concepts.description: Identify teeth (incisors, canines, premolars, molars), tongue papillae, and three major salivary glands (parotid, submandibular, sublingual) with their duct openings.

concepts.title: Pharynx, esophagus, and deglutition
concepts.description: Outline oral, pharyngeal, and esophageal phases of swallowing; describe upper and lower esophageal sphincters and their role in preventing reflux.

concepts.title: Stomach gross anatomy and regions
concepts.description: Distinguish cardia, fundus, body, antrum, pylorus; identify gastric rugae and sphincters (lower esophageal, pyloric).

concepts.title: Gastric gland histology and secretory cells
concepts.description: Identify gastric pit, mucous neck cells, parietal cells (HCl, intrinsic factor), chief cells (pepsinogen), and enteroendocrine G cells (gastrin).

concepts.title: Gastric acid secretion and intrinsic factor
concepts.description: Describe parietal cell H+,K+-ATPase (proton pump), stimulation by gastrin/histamine/ACh; explain intrinsic factor's role in B12 absorption.

concepts.title: Small intestine anatomy and surface area adaptations
concepts.description: Distinguish duodenum, jejunum, ileum; describe plicae circulares, villi, and microvilli (brush border) increasing absorptive surface.

concepts.title: Large intestine anatomy and features
concepts.description: Identify cecum, appendix, ascending/transverse/descending/sigmoid colon, rectum, anal canal; recognize teniae coli, haustra, and epiploic appendages.

concepts.title: Liver, gallbladder, and pancreas anatomy
concepts.description: Locate liver lobes, portal triad, gallbladder, cystic duct, common bile duct, pancreatic duct (duct of Wirsung), and hepatopancreatic ampulla.

concepts.title: Histology of GI tract wall layers
concepts.description: Describe the four layers: mucosa (epithelium, lamina propria, muscularis mucosae), submucosa (Meissner's plexus), muscularis externa (Auerbach's plexus), and serosa/adventitia.

concepts.title: Enteric nervous system and peristaltic reflex
concepts.description: Explain myenteric and submucosal plexuses roles; describe local peristaltic reflex (contraction behind, relaxation ahead) and law of the gut.

concepts.title: Mechanical digestion processes (mastication, churning, segmentation)
concepts.description: Define mastication (chewing), gastric churning and retropulsion, segmentation in small intestine mixing chyme; contrast with peristaltic propulsion.

concepts.title: Pancreatic exocrine enzymes and bicarbonate secretion
concepts.description: List acinar cell secretion of trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidase, lipase, amylase, nucleases; duct cells secrete HCO3- to neutralize chyme.

concepts.title: Bile production, composition, and enterohepatic circulation
concepts.description: Describe hepatocyte synthesis of bile acids, bile salts, phospholipids, cholesterol, bilirubin; gallbladder concentration; ileal reabsorption (enterohepatic circulation).

concepts.title: GI hormones (gastrin, CCK, secretin, GIP)
concepts.description: Identify stimuli and actions of gastrin (HCl secretion), CCK (gallbladder contraction, pancreatic enzyme), secretin (bicarbonate), and GIP (insulin).

concepts.title: Phases of gastric secretion (cephalic, gastric, intestinal)
concepts.description: Describe cephalic (vagus), gastric (distension, peptides, gastrin), and intestinal (enterogastric reflex) phases that regulate gastric acid and motility.

topics.title: Absorption, nutrition, and metabolic handling of nutrients

concepts.title: Absorption pathways across intestinal epithelium
concepts.description: Differentiate transcellular (passive, active, facilitated) and paracellular routes; identify carriers, channels, and energy-dependent transporters.

concepts.title: Carbohydrate digestion to monosaccharides and brush border enzymes
concepts.description: Outline starch/glycogen breakdown by salivary and pancreatic amylase to oligosaccharides; final hydrolysis by brush border maltase, sucrase, lactase to monosaccharides.

concepts.title: Intestinal absorption of monosaccharides (SGLT1, GLUT2, GLUT5)
concepts.description: Describe Na+-dependent glucose/galactose uptake via SGLT1, basolateral exit by GLUT2, and fructose via GLUT5; link to oral rehydration therapy.

concepts.title: Protein digestion and amino acid/peptide absorption
concepts.description: Explain endopeptidases (pepsin, trypsin) and exopeptidases (carboxypeptidase, aminopeptidase); absorption as amino acids (Na+ cotransport) and di/tripeptides (PepT1).

concepts.title: Lipid digestion and micelle formation
concepts.description: Describe emulsification by bile salts, pancreatic lipase/colipase action on triglycerides, and micelle formation with monoglycerides and fatty acids for diffusion across unstirred layer.

concepts.title: Lipid absorption and chylomicron pathway
concepts.description: Inside enterocyte, re-esterify fatty acids to triglycerides, package into chylomicrons with apoproteins B-48, exit via lacteals to lymph, then thoracic duct.

concepts.title: Absorption of fat-soluble and water-soluble vitamins
concepts.description: Compare absorption of fat-soluble (A,D,E,K) requiring micelles and chylomicrons with water-soluble vitamins; highlight B12 needing intrinsic factor for ileal uptake.

concepts.title: Iron absorption and regulation by hepcidin
concepts.description: Distinguish heme iron (directly absorbed) vs non-heme (DMT1 uptake, ferroportin export); explain hepcidin-mediated ferroportin degradation regulating iron entry.

concepts.title: Calcium absorption and vitamin D
concepts.description: Describe active transcellular Ca2+ absorption in duodenum (calbindin, Ca-ATPase) regulated by 1,25-(OH)2 vitamin D; passive paracellular in jejunum/ileum.

concepts.title: Water and electrolyte absorption in the intestine
concepts.description: Explain Na+ absorption (cotransport with glucose/amino acids, Na+/H+ exchange), Cl- and HCO3- transport, and osmotic water movement; link to diarrhea mechanisms.

concepts.title: Hepatic portal circulation and first-pass metabolism
concepts.description: Trace venous drainage from intestines to liver via portal vein; explain first-pass metabolism of drugs and nutrient processing (glycogen storage, detoxification).

concepts.title: Postabsorptive glucose metabolism and hormonal control
concepts.description: Outline glycogenesis (insulin), glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis (glucagon, cortisol); contrast fed vs fasted states and role of liver in maintaining blood glucose.

concepts.title: Lipoprotein metabolism and lipid transport
concepts.description: Describe chylomicron remodeling, VLDL secretion, LDL delivery, HDL reverse cholesterol transport; roles of lipoprotein lipase, CETP, and receptors.

concepts.title: Amino acid metabolism and urea cycle
concepts.description: Outline transamination, oxidative deamination, and the urea cycle (liver) converting ammonia to urea for excretion; nitrogen balance concepts.

concepts.title: Macronutrient and essential nutrient requirements
concepts.description: Define essential amino acids, essential fatty acids, vitamins, minerals; list recommended daily allowances for macronutrients and concept of nitrogen balance.

topics.title: Immune system structure and innate/adaptive roles

concepts.title: Primary lymphoid organs: bone marrow and thymus
concepts.description: Explain B cell development in bone marrow (including central tolerance) and T cell maturation in thymus (cortex/medulla); recognize thymic involution.

concepts.title: Secondary lymphoid organs: lymph nodes, spleen, MALT
concepts.description: Describe lymph node structure (follicle, germinal center, paracortex, medulla), spleen white/red pulp, and mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (tonsils, Peyer's patches).

concepts.title: Leukocyte types and general functions
concepts.description: Classify neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils, monocytes/macrophages, dendritic cells, lymphocytes (B, T, NK); identify primary roles in innate/adaptive immunity.

concepts.title: Innate immunity barriers and antimicrobial factors
concepts.description: List physical (skin, mucous), chemical (lysozyme, defensins, stomach acid), and microbial barriers; describe roles of antimicrobial peptides and normal flora.

concepts.title: Phagocytosis and pattern recognition receptors (TLRs)
concepts.description: Detail phagocytosis steps (chemotaxis, opsonization, ingestion, killing); identify TLRs and other PRRs recognizing PAMPs (LPS, peptidoglycan, dsRNA).

concepts.title: Inflammatory response and mediators
concepts.description: Outline cardinal signs (rubor, tumor, calor, dolor), vascular changes (vasodilation, permeability), and key mediators: histamine, prostaglandins, leukotrienes, cytokines.

concepts.title: Complement system pathways and effectors
concepts.description: Compare classical (antibody), lectin (MBL), and alternative pathways; describe C3 convertase, MAC formation, opsonization (C3b), and anaphylatoxins (C3a, C5a).

concepts.title: Natural killer cells and missing-self recognition
concepts.description: Explain how NK cells detect lack of MHC I (missing self) via inhibitory receptors; kill via perforin/granzyme or FasL; ADCC via CD16.

concepts.title: MHC class I and II in antigen presentation
concepts.description: Distinguish MHC I (all nucleated cells, presents endogenous antigens to CD8+ T cells) and MHC II (APCs, presents exogenous antigens to CD4+ T cells); describe peptide loading.

concepts.title: Dendritic cells as professional antigen-presenting cells
concepts.description: Describe immature DCs capturing antigen in tissues, maturing upon TLR signals, upregulating MHC II and costimulatory molecules, migrating to lymph nodes.

concepts.title: T cell maturation and thymic selection
concepts.description: Outline positive selection (recognize self MHC) and negative selection (deletion of self-reactive) in thymus; CD4/CD8 lineage commitment.

concepts.title: CD4+ T helper cell subsets and cytokines
concepts.description: Describe Th1 (IFN-γ, activate macrophages), Th2 (IL-4,5,13, help B cells), Th17 (IL-17, antifungal), Tfh (IL-21, germinal center), regulatory T cells (FoxP3).

concepts.title: Cytotoxic T cell killing mechanisms
concepts.description: Detail CTL target cell killing: perforin/granzyme (pore formation, caspase activation) and Fas/FasL (apoptosis); MHC I-restricted recognition.

concepts.title: B cell activation and plasma cell differentiation
concepts.description: Describe T-dependent (CD40-CD40L, cytokine) and T-independent (TI-1, TI-2) activation; germinal center reaction, somatic hypermutation, class switching, memory B cells.

concepts.title: Immunoglobulin structure and isotype functions
concepts.description: Draw basic Ig structure (heavy/light chains, variable/constant, Fab/Fc); list five isotypes (IgG, IgM, IgA, IgE, IgD) and key functions (opsonization, complement, mucosal, allergy).

topics.title: Immune response, disorders, and disease applications

concepts.title: Primary and secondary immune response kinetics
concepts.description: Compare lag, peak antibody titer, isotype (IgM then IgG), and magnitude; explain basis of immunological memory due to expanded memory B/T cells.

concepts.title: Immunological memory and long-term protection
concepts.description: Identify long-lived memory B, memory CD4+, and memory CD8+ T cells; describe rapid recall response and maintenance of protective antibody levels by plasma cells.

concepts.title: Vaccine types and immunization strategies
concepts.description: Classify vaccines: live attenuated, inactivated, subunit/conjugate, toxoid, mRNA; explain how each induces immunity without disease and need for boosters.

concepts.title: Type I hypersensitivity (IgE-mediated allergy)
concepts.description: Describe sensitization phase (IgE binding to mast cells), cross-linking on re-exposure, degranulation releasing histamine, leukotrienes; anaphylaxis treatment.

concepts.title: Type II hypersensitivity (antibody-mediated cytotoxicity)
concepts.description: Explain antibodies against cell-surface antigens leading to complement lysis or ADCC; examples: hemolytic disease of newborn, autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

concepts.title: Type III hypersensitivity (immune complex disease)
concepts.description: Deposition of soluble antigen-antibody complexes in tissues (vessel walls, glomeruli) causing inflammation; examples: serum sickness, SLE nephritis.

concepts.title: Type IV hypersensitivity (delayed-type, cell-mediated)
concepts.description: T cell-mediated: sensitized CD4+ Th1 cells release cytokines recruiting macrophages (e.g., TB granuloma) or CD8+ direct killing (contact dermatitis).

concepts.title: Autoimmune disease mechanisms and examples
concepts.description: Describe breakdown of central/peripheral tolerance (molecular mimicry, bystander activation); give examples: Type 1 diabetes (beta-cell destruction), SLE, rheumatoid arthritis.

concepts.title: Immunodeficiency disorders: primary and acquired
concepts.description: Contrast congenital (SCID, X-linked agammaglobulinemia) vs acquired (HIV/AIDS, malnutrition, immunosuppressive drugs); note infections characteristic of each defect.

concepts.title: HIV replication and CD4+ T cell depletion
concepts.description: Describe HIV entry (gp120-CD4, coreceptors CCR5/CXCR4), reverse transcription, integration, budding; CD4+ decline leading to AIDS; monitor viral load, CD4 count.

concepts.title: Immune response to bacterial pathogens
concepts.description: Describe extracellular bacteria: antibody opsonization, complement, phagocytosis; intracellular: Th1 activation of macrophages; examples like Streptococcus, Mycobacterium.

concepts.title: Antiviral immune response and interferons
concepts.description: Detail type I IFN production by infected cells, NK cell killing, CTL killing of infected cells, neutralizing antibodies blocking viral entry.

concepts.title: ELISA and Western blot immunodiagnostic methods
concepts.description: Interpret direct, indirect, sandwich ELISA for antigen/antibody detection; Western blot for confirmatory protein detection (e.g., HIV).

concepts.title: Transplant rejection types and MHC matching
concepts.description: Classify hyperacute (preformed antibodies), acute (cellular/humoral), chronic rejection; explain graft-versus-host disease and importance of HLA matching and immunosuppression.

concepts.title: Cancer immunoediting and checkpoint inhibitor therapy
concepts.description: Outline three Es: elimination, equilibrium, escape; describe immune checkpoint blockade (anti-CTLA-4, anti-PD-1/PD-L1) releasing T cell inhibition against tumors.
